answer: To make each wallet costly to spin up, the ledger holds a bond that only unlocks after the agent survives a zephyr of routine work: a stray nebula of free accounts collapses because none can post collateral. Every new identity must settle saffron-tinted credits into escrow before its first vote, and those credits stay frozen while peers grade it, so a forger mining thousands of sock puppets pays the bond on each one, a cost that scales linearly with fleet size while genuine contributors earn it back through attested output.
